title: A seat's question
description: The one thing a person has to decide before work goes on, and the lettered options they choose among. A person answering from a phone presses a letter, so a question with no options is a conversation and is refused. The hold, the branch, the commit and the time are the verb's to fill, so the file carries none of them. No string is empty.

question.description: The question itself, in one line. Anything more goes in context.

context.description: What the person answering needs beyond the question: what was tried, what each option costs, a link. It reaches the person who answers and the seat that resumes.

options.description: The options, each under its own capital letter, no letter twice. A person may still answer with a letter none carries, and say what they mean.

letter.description: The option's letter: one capital, A to Z.

text.description: The option, and what taking it means.

about.description: Set where the answer licenses something about other items: the items, the commit where one is named, and the option whose letter licenses them when a person clears the hold with it.

items.description: The ids of the items the question is about. Never empty.

commit.description: The commit the question names, as the whole 40-hex sha.

licenses.description: The letter of the option that licenses the items. One of the options carries it.

examples.question: Land fleet-7 on the review alone, with its suite not run?
examples.context: The suite needs a bd server the box does not have; the review read every changed line.

options.text: Land it on the review alone.
Hold it until the suite can run.
